classification.difficultyReason: Compare the vertex and interval endpoints, recognising when the vertex lies outside the specified domain.

content.prompt: What is the maximum and minimum value of $3x^2+7x-2$ if:

answer.worked:
Let $f(x)=3x^2+7x-2$. The parabola opens upwards. Its axis of symmetry is
$$\begin{align*}x&=-\frac{7}{2\times3}\\x&=-\frac76.\end{align*}$$
The vertex lies in $[-3,0]$. Compare the vertex and endpoints:
$$\begin{align*}f\left(-\frac76\right)&=3\left(-\frac76\right)^2+7\left(-\frac76\right)-2\\f\left(-\frac76\right)&=-\frac{73}{12}\\f(-3)&=3(-3)^2+7(-3)-2=4\\f(0)&=-2.\end{align*}$$
The maximum is $4$ at $x=-3$, and the minimum is $-\dfrac{73}{12}$ at $x=-\dfrac76$.

Let $f(x)=3x^2+7x-2$. The parabola opens upwards, with axis of symmetry
$$\begin{align*}x&=-\frac{7}{2\times3}\\x&=-\frac76.\end{align*}$$
The interval $[0,3]$ lies to the right of the vertex, where the parabola rises. Thus the endpoint values give the minimum and maximum:
$$\begin{align*}f(0)&=-2\\f(3)&=3(3)^2+7(3)-2\\f(3)&=46.\end{align*}$$
The maximum is $46$ at $x=3$, and the minimum is $-2$ at $x=0$.
